transcribed_question:
A) Identify the bone (be specific)
B) Identify the area painted blue and what does it articulate with

marker.description: Blue paint marking on the left side of the vertebra.

main_question: Identify the bone and the blue-painted area, and state what it articulates with.
main_answer: Lumbar vertebra; the blue-painted area is the superior articular facet, which articulates with the inferior articular facet of the vertebra above.
main_explanation: The specimen is a vertebra with a large vertebral body and a triangular vertebral foramen, consistent with a lumbar vertebra. The blue mark is on an articular process/facet region; on this view it most likely indicates a superior articular facet, which forms a zygapophysial joint with the inferior articular facet of the vertebra above.

supporting_question.question: Which feature best distinguishes a lumbar vertebra from a thoracic vertebra?
supporting_question.explanation: Lumbar vertebrae have large kidney-shaped bodies and lack costal facets and transverse foramina.

true_false.statement: Lumbar vertebrae articulate with each other at the zygapophysial joints formed by the articular facets.
true_false.explanation: Adjacent vertebrae meet at paired synovial facet joints, also called zygapophysial joints.
